title: Project Management — Certificate Program
tagline: Plan, coordinate and improve delivery with Agile, Scrum, risk discipline and Jira — backed by an evidence-led portfolio.
audience: Beginner undergraduate learners (B.Com, BBA, BA, B.Sc) preparing for Project Coordinator, PMO Analyst, Operations Associate roles. No coding or prior industry experience required.
language: English; reflections and presentations may be in Kannada or Hindi by arrangement
weeklyCommitment: 6 hours per week: guided practice, independent study and portfolio projects
certificateTitle: Project Management Practice — Certificate of Completion
prerequisites: Basic arithmetic, percentages and comfort with spreadsheets or a willingness to learn
Access to a browser or shared college computer; offline spreadsheet alternatives are accepted
No paid tool subscription, live client account or real personal dataset required
outcomes: Translate a request into a charter, scope boundary, stakeholder map and measurable acceptance criteria.
Build a work breakdown, dependency schedule and cost forecast with explicit assumptions.
Apply Agile and Scrum concepts appropriately, including goals, accountabilities and the Definition of Done.
Use Jira or an equivalent board to manage backlog items, dependencies, filters and workflow evidence.
Maintain risk, issue, quality and change records and escalate decisions within authority.
Produce reconciled PMO status reports and support portfolio and benefits reviews.
Plan vendor coordination, SOPs and operational handover with realistic capacity and controls.
Present an honest portfolio for Project Coordinator, PMO Analyst and Operations Associate interviews.

conditions: At least three of four Project Blocks submitted
At least 75% attendance for instructor-led cohorts
Institutional award requires facilitator marking and integrity clearance; platform eligibility alone is not the award

components.name: Lesson quizzes
components.description: Best-attempt percentage averaged equally over all 24 lesson quizzes, scaled to 15 marks.

components.name: Project Blocks 1–4
components.description: Four applied portfolio projects, each marked out of 7 using the published rubric.

components.name: Capstone and presentation
components.description: An integrated simulation with traceable evidence, a five-minute pitch and individual questions.

components.name: Final assessment
components.description: A 90-minute assessment: 40 MCQs and two applied cases, scaled from 100 to 20 marks.

components.name: Reflection journal
components.description: Evidence of corrections, professional judgement and learning across all modules.

tools: Google Docs or a local word processor
toolkit.note: All calculations and templates can be completed offline.
No paid feature or live organisational Jira access is required; interfaces and free-tier availability vary.
Use synthetic data; do not publish credentials or confidential records.

modules.title: Project foundations and stakeholder decisions
modules.summary: Translate a business request into a bounded project, an approval route and a measurable definition of success.
outcomes: Distinguish a temporary project from ongoing operations and separate outputs from intended benefits.
Write a charter that makes authority, boundaries and acceptance testable.
Map stakeholder needs and assign decision responsibilities without overloading every meeting.
